name: Softgenlab Temporary Login Links
author: softgenlab

sections.description:
Need to let a developer, designer or support agent into your WordPress site? Stop sharing your admin password or creating accounts you forget to delete.

This plugin creates a private login link with the permissions you choose. When the time is up, the link stops working and the person is logged out.

Features

  • Temporary login links – from 1 hour to 90 days, with no password needed.
  • Expires automatically – expired users are logged out on their next request and removed after a week.
  • Extend, renew or revoke access with one click.
  • Role editor with ready-made presets: Website work (content, design and products, without code, settings, orders, customers or users), Plugins, and Content only.
  • Clear labels show which permissions reveal orders, customers or user accounts, and which can change code or settings.
  • Activity log of logins, changes and blocked attempts, stored on your own site.
  • Works with WooCommerce.

How this plugin protects your site

  • Temporary users can only log in with their link – never with a password, password reset or application password.
  • Expired or revoked users are treated as logged out on every route: normal pages, the dashboard, admin-ajax, the REST API and XML-RPC.
  • Temporary users cannot create, promote or edit user accounts, and cannot deactivate this plugin from the Plugins screen.
  • You can only give out, renew or extend access with permissions you have yourself.
  • Link tokens are 256-bit random values. The database stores only a keyed hash of each token. Right after you create a link, an encrypted copy is kept for up to 5 minutes so it can be shown to you once; the key to decrypt it is held only in your browser, and the copy is deleted as soon as it is shown.
  • Login cookies never last longer than the access itself.
  • Invalid links are rate limited per IP address.
  • If you deactivate this plugin, every temporary account is locked: its roles are set aside, its password is replaced with an unknown random one (cancelling any password reset), and its sessions, application passwords and link are removed. Reactivating gives the roles back; links stay off until you create new ones.
  • This plugin makes no external requests.

What expiry can and cannot do

Expiry ends someone’s access. It cannot undo what they did while they had it.

Anyone you give code-level permissions – installing, activating or editing plugins and themes, editing files, unfiltered HTML, importing, or changing site settings – can make changes that stay on the site after their access ends, and could use those changes to get back in or to reach data their role does not show. This plugin cannot prevent that. This plugin asks you to confirm before creating a login with these permissions. Only give them to people you trust, and review the site when the work is done.

The “Website work” and “Content only” presets leave these permissions out. The “Plugins” preset includes them, and says so.

Pro version

The Pro version adds one-time links, IP restrictions, scheduled access, blocked areas, email and Slack alerts, emailing links to your developer, CSV export of the activity log, white label and priority support. Your temporary logins carry over when you upgrade, and the free version switches itself off while Pro is active.

Credits and licenses

This plugin is released under the GPLv2 or later. All code, styles and artwork in this plugin, including the logo (assets/logo.png), are original work by Softgenlab and are released under the same license. It uses no third-party libraries; link encryption uses the libsodium functions built into PHP and WordPress.
sections.installation:
1. Go to Plugins → Add New, search for “Softgenlab Temporary Login Links”, then install and activate it.
  2. Open Temporary Logins in the admin menu.
  3. Enter who the access is for, choose a role and how long it should last, then click Create access link.
  4. Copy the link and send it privately.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin let an outside service manage my site?

No. There is no remote service, account, API or server involved, and the plugin makes no outside connections. A link is created by an administrator of your own site, for one person that administrator chooses, with only the permissions that administrator picks (never more than they have themselves). The link works only on your site, expires on its own, and can be revoked at any time. Nobody can create or use a link without being logged in to your site as an administrator.

Do temporary users need a password?

No. They log in with their private link only. Password logins and password resets are blocked for temporary accounts.

What happens when access expires?

The link stops working and the person is logged out on their next request. Expired logins are deleted automatically after 7 days, and any content they created is given to the person who created the login, or to an administrator.

Can a temporary user give themselves permanent access?

Not through user accounts: temporary users cannot create or edit users, create application passwords, reset passwords or deactivate this plugin from the Plugins screen.

But if their role can change code or site settings (for example install or edit plugins, edit theme files, or change who can register), they could add code or settings that keep working after their access ends. Expiry cannot undo those changes. Use the “Website work” or “Content only” preset unless the person really needs that level of access, and only give it to people you trust.

Can I hide WooCommerce orders and customers?

Yes. Create a role with the “Website work” preset, which leaves out orders, customers, user accounts, code and settings, then choose that role for the temporary login. A role that can change code is never labelled “Customer data hidden”, because code access can be used to reach that data.

Who can renew or extend a login?

Only someone who has every permission that login has. A user who can manage temporary logins cannot renew, extend or take over one that is more powerful than they are.

I lost the link. Can I see it again?

For security, links are shown only once. Click “New link” to create a fresh one; the old link stops working.

What data does this plugin store?

Everything stays in your own WordPress database:

  • For each temporary login: a label, the expiry time, who created it, the last login time and a hash of the link token.
  • An activity log of the last 200 events (logins, created, extended, revoked and deleted logins, role changes and blocked link attempts). Each entry stores the time, the login’s label, the admin who acted and the visitor’s IP address. You can clear it at any time under Activity.

Nothing is sent to other servers.

What happens if I deactivate the plugin?

All temporary accounts are locked (no roles, unknown random password, no sessions, application passwords or links), so nobody can use them while this plugin is off. Reactivate this plugin to give the roles back, then create new links.

What happens if I delete the plugin?

If the Pro version is active, nothing shared is deleted, because Pro is still using the temporary logins, roles list and log. Otherwise all temporary users are deleted (their content is given to the person who created the login, or the first administrator) and this plugin’s data and activity log are removed. If there is no administrator to receive a temporary user’s content, that user is locked instead of deleted so nothing is lost. Custom roles you created are kept, because other users may have them.
sections.changelog:
1.0.3

  • Renamed to “Softgenlab Temporary Login Links” (new text domain and support address). No other change to how it works.
  • Core admin files are no longer loaded where WordPress has already loaded them.

1.0.2

  • Security: deactivating this plugin now also sets aside extra capabilities given directly to a temporary account, and clears its email address so no password reset can be sent while the plugin is off. Temporary accounts can no longer save an email address.
  • Security: handing out or managing access now respects permission limits that other plugins apply only to you.
  • Security: logins created in the Pro version with one-time, IP, schedule or blocked-area limits are refused by the free version (which cannot enforce those limits) instead of working without them. They can be revoked or deleted here, or used again once Pro is active.

1.0.1

  • Security: renewing, extending, revoking or deleting a login now needs every permission that login has.
  • Security: the free version now reliably stays off while the Pro version is active, whatever order plugins load in.
  • Security: the “Website work” preset no longer includes code or settings permissions. Roles that can change code are labelled as such, and creating a login with them needs a confirmation.
  • Security: deactivating this plugin now locks every temporary account instead of only logging it out.
  • Security: expired or revoked users are rejected on every request type, including the REST API, admin-ajax and XML-RPC.
  • Security: the one-time copy of a new link is now stored encrypted, with the key held only in your browser.
  • Uninstall keeps shared data only while the Pro version is active, and never deletes content when there is nobody to give it to.
  • Other plugins’ notices are no longer hidden on the plugin screen.
  • Clearer documentation of what expiry can and cannot undo, and of the data this plugin stores.

1.0.0

  • First release.
